evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: `oc get applicationset agentit-managed-apps -o jsonpath='{.spec.strategy}'` → empty; states strategy absent means AllAtOnce and refuses to fabricate a RollingSync status block.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: No steps exist to map. Explains matchExpressions-based step selection and notes the generated template stamps no env label, so a production matchExpressions selector would match zero Applications — but cannot identify an actual group.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'maxUpdate slots occupied by unhealthy apps' and the Healthy+Synced gate as causes to walk, but no maxUpdate value or gate state could be checked (no strategy, no apps).

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Runs the per-step health query (`-l app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=applicationset-controller -o custom-columns=NAME,SYNC,HEALTH`) which returns no rows, and names it as the view that would show the blocked step; no actual staging app health was debugged because none exist.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: "RollingSync advances only when every Application in the prior step is Healthy and Synced"; also notes automated syncPolicy is required for progression.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: States the premise does not hold, ranks three explanations (strategy never applied, applied to an instance with no appset controller, or the label/selector gap) with prioritized proposals.

expectations.evidence: After confirming checkout-api/prod do not exist, dumps bluegreen-demo .spec.strategy.blueGreen (activeService, previewService, autoPromotionEnabled true, autoPromotionSeconds 30) and .status.blueGreen selectors.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: "autoPromotionEnabled: false means the Rollout will sit at preview indefinitely... One hour is not a timeout; there is no timeout" and "autoPromotionEnabled does not control analysis" — explicitly separates the two settings.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: Confirms no prePromotionAnalysis/postPromotionAnalysis on the real Rollout and no AnalysisRun ever created for it; gives the single jsonpath that settles it and ranks 'prePromotionAnalysis configured but AnalysisRun Running/Error' as cause 2 with the AnalysisRun query.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: Lists both Services and their endpoints (both resolve to 10.129.2.9:8080), explains active==preview selector is expected at revision 1, and flags the preview-equals-production consequence.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: Notes the canary-centric pause/analysis/setWeight step fields do not apply; for blue-green the operative fields are autoPromotionEnabled, autoPromotionSeconds, prePromotionAnalysis.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Concludes behaviour is correct-as-configured (BLOCKER: none), ranks causes to rule out, and gives prioritized proposals plus the (unexecuted) promote command.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: "Suspended is not a failure state" — cites the status table and names CronJob spec.suspend:true and a paused Rollout (spec.paused / indefinite pause step) as the producers.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource to identify what is suspended and why

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: "BLOCKER — none. Suspended is a reported state, not a fault"; warns that unsuspending a CronJob in-cluster would be reverted by selfHeal if it is deliberate in Git.

expectations.text: Produces a report distinguishing intentional suspension from a genuine problem
expectations.evidence: Separates Suspended from sync-window denial explicitly ('a sync window produces SyncWindow: Sync Denied and leaves health untouched; it does not produce Suspended health') and from the wrong-instance-namespace lookup error, with evidence from the example-team AppProject windows.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Runs the discriminator on every Application (`{.spec.sources}` vs `{.spec.source.repoURL}`) and on the real object, returning 'single-source' with status.sourceType Kustomize; reports no multi-source Application exists rather than inventing one.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Supplies the per-source enumeration `{range .spec.sources[*]}repoURL= targetRevision= path= chart= ref= valueFiles=…{end}` covering every required field; no entries existed to iterate.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: No failing source exists. Gives five ranked causes (missing/mismatched `ref` + `$values`, valueFiles resolved from the wrong root, chart-version drift, divergent revisions, per-repo credentials) each with its check, and uses `.status.sync.comparedTo.sources[]` vs `.spec.sources[]` to localise the index — but no specific source is identified.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Treats the topology explicitly: ref source feeding `$values/...` into the chart render, and warns the two sources are not rendered independently so errors are attributed to the Application, not a source index.

expectations.text: Produces a report identifying the specific failing source and the fix
expectations.evidence: Full report with isolation procedure and prioritized fixes (declare ref, pin both targetRevisions, compare comparedTo.sources, add repo credentials), but no specific failing source because none exists on the cluster.
